  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  September 13, 2021
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:03 p.m., on Monday, September 13, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met in
Council Chambers and virtually via Zoom.

PRESENT:  LEE
PRESENT via Zoom:  MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present in person and via Zoom: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes,
Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance
Lieu, Director of Public Works/ Utilities Ray, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of
Library LohGuan, Marketing and Communications Specialist Nguyen, Director of Community
Development Ho, Principal Planner Lam, Assistant Planner Abrego, Fire Chief Phelps, Police
Chief Parra, Director of Human Resources Ko

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-113

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the regular meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor in accordance with Section 54955 and
54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES
Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council
taking action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may
determine that the title has been read.

Action Taken:  On motion of Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, seconded by Ms. LEE, the City
Council determined that the titles to all ordinances which appeared on this public agenda had
been read, and waived further reading. Hearing no objections, the Mayor so ordered.

Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded: LEE
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DECISION APPROVING A REVISION

  1
9-13-21
   TO CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CUP-20-02 TO ALLOW A CHANGE OF HOURS OF
  OPERATION AT AN EXISTING 1,924 SQUARE FOOT BUILDING ON AN
  APPROXIMATE LAND AREA OF 4,128 SQUARE FEET LOCATED IN THE CBD-DRD
  (CENTRAL BUSINESS DISTRICT - DOWNTOWN REVITALIZATION DISTRICT) ZONE
  – F2M21-61, N2M21-108, M2M21-116

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M21-108 for the City Council to hold a
  public hearing regarding an appeal filed by Christian Yang (Liao Marcos Yang LLC dba
  Yang’s Kitchen) of the Planning Commission’s decision approving a revision to Conditional
  Use Permit CUP-20-02 to allow a change of hours of operation at Yang’s Kitchen
  restaurant. Specifically, the Appellant appealed Conditions of Approval PL1, PL2 and
  PL6 to Conditional Use Permit CUP-20-02 limiting business hours to 7:00 a.m. to 12:00
  a.m., Monday through Sunday, instead of the 7:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. as originally
  requested by the Appellant. Director of Community Development HO introduced Assistant
  Planner ABREGO who delivered a staff report and a presentation which is on file in the
  City Clerk’s office.

  The Appellant, Mr. YANG discussed the background of the restaurant, the challenges
  faced during the COVID-19 pandemic and the ways in which they sought to keep the
  business going. He explained his reasons for requesting the appeal to the Conditions of
  Approval.

  Open Public Hearing:  Mayor Lee opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:  John BWARIE, representing Alhambra Chamber of Commerce,
  spoke in favor of the appellant as member of the business community and supported the
  extended hours.

  Close Public Hearing: After receiving public comment, Mayor Lee closed the public
  hearing.

  Discussion: Council discussed the proximity of Yang’s Kitchen to housing units and the
  ways in which the restaurant adapted to the COVID-19 pandemic shortly after opening.
  Councilmembers MAZA, PÉREZ, and MALONEY discussed the importance of supporting
  businesses in light of the pandemic, the importance of successful restaurants in drawing
  new visitors to Alhambra, and their support of Yang’s Kitchen who they believed would
  utilize a CUP with responsibility. Mr. YANG further explained that the restaurant sought a
  CUP to offer greater flexibility to their business and to allow for special events which were
  still being planned. Mr. MAZA and Mr. MALONEY pointed out that CUP’s could be revoked
  by the Planning Commission and Council should there be any complaints from residents.
  Councilmembers MAZA, PÉREZ, and MALONEY supported granting the Appeal and
  waiving the fees for appeal.

  Mayor LEE, Mr. YANG, Mr. HO, and Mr. LAM discussed the nature of the restaurant, the
  hours of operation for other restaurants and bars which serve food items, and Mr. Yang’s
  plans for the restaurant. Ms. LEE explained that she understood the concerns of the
  Planning Commission raised during their public hearing and was hesitant to grant the
  appeal given the lack of specific information regarding the special events at this time. She
  stated that she would be comfortable extending the hours of operation only on specific
  nights to accommodate special events.

  2
9-13-21
   Action Taken:  City Council directed staff to return at the next City Council meeting
  with a Resolution granting the Appeal and approving the revision of conditions of approval
  for Conditional Use Permit CUP-20-02 for hours of operation between 7:00 a.m. to 2:00
  a.m. and waive fees for appeal. (M2M21-116)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded: PÉREZ
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY
  Noes:  LEE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

2.  2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE OF THE ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN –
  F2M20-37

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report and introduced Chris
  BLAKNEY, Project Director from ECONorthwest who presented to the City Council an
  update on the 2021-2029 Housing Element Update Project of the Alhambra General Plan.
  The presentation provided an update and overview of the status of the Housing Element.

  Public Comment:

  1) Ari ARAMBULA expressed concerns regarding the public noticing for the discussion
  at the City Council meeting. She reported on her experience in the presentation
  described by Mr. Blakney and stated that the lengthy document needed more
  explanation to the public than a 20-minute PowerPoint presentation. She stressed the
  need for more community engagement and explanation at a higher level. She further
  discussed the need to assure affordable housing is developed in Alhambra.

  2) Lewis MCCAMMON discussed the Housing Element Update, the RHNA cycle 5 and
  6 targets for low and extremely low housing, the work to preserve rental units with
  expiring affordable housing units, the inability to meet the RHNA cycle 6 goals, the
  current affordable housing developments,

  3) John BWARIE, CEO of the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce, stated that the Chamber
  was working with the City to provide input regarding the need for housing, to support
  businesses which would further attract residents to the city, and asked that the City
  continue to work with the business community to help support the local economy
  through housing development.

  4) Salvador GEORGE, representing the Southwest Regional Council of Carpenters,
  supported development and stressed the importance of a local hiring policy for current
  and future development projects.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ requested that the City pursue Affordable Housing
  Overlay for the entire city and stated that the City needed to offer as many affordable
  housing options as possible. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER requested that the
  City revisit the Community Workforce Agreement and the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance

  3
9-13-21
   to see how they could be strengthened. Councilmember MALONEY and Mr. BLAKNEY
  discussed housing possibilities in the industrial areas in Alhambra and the conversion of
  underutilized or commercial industrial buildings. Mayor LEE and Mr. BLAKNEY discussed
  public outreach and participation in the public workshops, California State bills SB9 and
  SB10, State Assembly Member Chu’s AB215 which would strengthen the enforcement of
  RHNA goals, and the population density of Alhambra and neighboring cities.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

3.  SAN GABRIEL VALLEY REGIONAL HOUSING TRUST FUND UPDATE – F2M20-27

  Brielle Acevedo, Housing Trust Administrator, from The San Gabriel Valley Regional
  Housing Trust (SGVRHT) presented to the City Council the accomplishments of the
  SGVRHT over the past year and plans for the year ahead. The presentation is on file in
  the City Clerk’s office.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis MCCAMMON spoke in favor of the Trust Fund and for the projects outlined in
  the presentation. He requested more information about the city of El Monte’s program
  to allow for residents to build Accessory Dwelling Units at no cost.

  Discussion: Council supported the Trust Fund and offered comments expressing
  gratitude for the working being done. Council briefly discussed the upcoming Mariposa
  affordable housing project and the potential funding it may receive. Council also briefly
  discussed upcoming legislature which may grant additional funds.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

4.  EAST MAIN CORRIDOR UPDATE – F2M21-60, F2M20-24, F2M14-55

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report. The East Main
  Commercial Zone or (EMC) was established in July 2015 and consists of properties
  located along Main Street from Garfield Avenue to the east City limits. It is commonly
  referred to as the East Main Corridor. Prior to the establishment of the EMC, the previous
  zoning classification for the corridor allowed for hotels, motels, and high- density
  residential uses. By establishing the EMC zone, the City determined it was not appropriate
  to allow hotels, motels, and high-density residential zoning along Main Street from Chapel
  Avenue to the eastern City limits. The vision and direction for the EMC is rooted in the
  General Plan. In August 2019, the City adopted the Alhambra General Plan Vision 2040
  which set forth a number of goals, polices and implementations actions. As it related to
  the EMC, one of the General Plan goals was to enhance community identification through
  the provision of signs, monuments, landscaping, or buildings, or a combination thereof at
  City gateways (General Plan Goal LU-5: Gateways). There were three policies associated
  with the aforementioned goal, including implementing a unified sign program to help orient
  visitors throughout the community (Policy LU-5A), incorporating unified design materials
  to provide a consistent brand identity and design (Policy LU-5B), and establish gateway
  treatments at key locations (Policy LU-5C). The implementation action of these goals and
  policies as it related to the EMC was to work with the surrounding community on a potential

  4
9-13-21
   Specific Plan for the East Main corridor, addressing issues, height, and design guidelines.
  On multiple occasions, community residents inquired about the progress in meeting the
  vision and implementation actions set by the General Plan. Specifically, inquiries focused
  on the East Main Street corridor as it related to community character and greater economic
  activity east of the City’s downtown. Roger Dale, of Natelson Dale Group, presented to
  the City Council an update on the City’s ongoing work effort as it related to the East Main
  Corridor. Topics included, but were not limited to: Current Status of EMC, Market Analysis;
  Pro-forma Analysis; Fiscal Impact Analysis; Next Steps; and Tentative Milestones for the
  EMC. The presentation is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  Public Comment:

  The following people spoke in favor a building moratorium for structures over 25
  feet in height, questioned some of the content of the report presented, spoke in
  favor of the creation of an Old Town Alhambra district, and advocated for more
  community input:

  1)  Olga Alarid
  2)  Brad Michaels
  3)  Marisol Grier
  4)  Ari Arambula
  5)  Jacob Mojarro
  6)  Lewis McCammon
  7)  Cody Corbett

  Additional Public Comment:

  1) John BWARIE, representing the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce, stated that the
  report was valuable to help the community decide how to move forward to address
  the economy of Southern California with regards to housing and retail development.

  Public Comment received via email on file in the City Clerk’s office:

  The following people spoke in favor of a building moratorium for structures over 25
  feet in height, spoke in favor of the creation of an Old Town Alhambra district, and
  spoke in favor of a Specific Development and Design Plan:

  1) Melissa Michelson
  2) Ngan Kwong
  3) Andrea Giese
  4) Jed Giese
  5) Lori Nelson
  6) Anthony Gutierrez
  7) Daniel Tong
  8) James Rojas
  9) Teresa Lucky
  10) Marina Gomez
  11) Laura Freeborn
  12) Jennifer Horen
  13) Elizabeth Mojarro Huang
  14) Shirley Tatsuno

  5
9-13-21
   15) Linda McClain
  16) Cat McCune
  17) Pamela Boucher
  18) Kevin McCune
  19) Jackie Robles
  20) Daniel and Marisela Díaz
  21) Jose G. Gomez
  22) Patty Gonzalez

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ and Director of Community Development HO
  discussed the various city planning tools and strategies for accomplishing the key goals
  identified by the community in their preferences for the East Main Corridor such as limiting
  physical development and building height, a cohesive architectural style and theme,
  streamlined development processes for specific businesses. Mr. HO explained the
  differences between past practices of Specific Plans and more modern practices of Zoning
  Code Updates, which the City was in process of examining, and Design Guidelines which
  was also being considered by City contracted consultants. Mr. Ho stated that land use
  has started to comingle more in recent years by the use of overlay districts and cities have
  incorporated zoning code updates to be more flexible and dynamic to adapt to changing
  times and land use.

  Ms. PÉREZ, Mr. HO, and City Attorney MONTES further addressed topics brought up in
  public comment and discussed the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (IHO) and the
  Community Workforce Agreement (CWA) as they related to publicly funded or sponsored
  projects versus private development projects.

  Ms. PÉREZ, Mr. HO, City Manager BINNQUIST discussed a previous Council meeting
  from September 2020 in which Council discussed the idea of a Specific Plan for the East
  Main Corridor and directed staff to move forward with an economic feasibility study and
  design guidelines. Councilmember MALONEY provided his recollection of the discussion
  and their budgetary concerns in 2020.

  Ms. PÉREZ went on to discuss the need for community outreach to address concerns of
  community and to reach wider groups. She discussed current outreach methods for the
  Zoning Code Update with Mr. Dale and Mr. Ho. Ms. PÉREZ suggested hosting in person
  meetings in outdoor settings and during the day to reach more of the senior population.

  Ms. PÉREZ and Mayor LEE discussed concerns regarding the proposed medical center
  in the East Main Corridor. Ms. LEE explained that she was concerned that there was no
  plan in place for the East Main Corridor, insufficient public input and discussion, and that
  a medical center does not match the proposed guideline for that segment of the corridor.
  Ms. PÉREZ reported that the project was being developed by the Chinatown Service
  Center and praised the organization for their leadership, successful history in the City,
  and their various low-cost health and medical services offered to low income residents
  with a focus on the API community. She stated that this was a positive development for
  the City that would provide valuable services to the community and that the project did not
  plan to increase their building height.
  Councilmember MAZA discussed the need to balance the need for additional housing and
  community needs to support residential neighborhoods. He stated that he supported the
  concept of an Old Town Alhambra, but added that the City needed to attract developers
  to make it happen. He stressed the need for increased community input to be incorporated

  6
9-13-21
   in the plans being made and suggested additional outreach to the community.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the lack of trust in the community and
  stated that it would behoove Natelson Dale Group to work with the neighbors so that the
  work is clear to residents. She discussed Mr. Dale’s report and the Old Town Alhambra
  suggestion. She questioned the purpose of a building moratorium, referred to Ms. Pérez’s
  discussion of the CWA, discussed the differences between a CWA and a Living Wage
  Ordinance with Mr. Montes, and requested an update of the CWA at a future Council
  meeting. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER went on to discuss Chinatown Service Center and
  the types of services they have provided to the community from their other location in the
  City.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. LEE discussed her support of the building moratorium
  in the East Main Corridor. Ms. LEE explained that her rational was based on the as of yet
  incomplete Economic Analysis and Architectural Design Guidelines for the East Main
  Corridor. Ms. Lee explained that without these two pieces finalized, it did not make sense
  to approve projects that may not conform to the Design Guidelines or the overall plan for
  the East Main Corridor. She referred to two projects in process, discussed their stages of
  approval with Mr. Ho, and concluded that a moratorium was necessary to temporarily halt
  the approval process for new projects until plans for the East Main Corridor have been
  finalized. Mr. MONTES clarified the purpose, process, and timeline of a moratorium
  ordinance.

  Councilmember MALONEY and Mr. HO continued to discuss modern city planning
  methods, use of specific plans in city planning, and examples of specific plans in cities
  such as Pasadena to create Old Town Pasadena beginning in the 1970s and 80s. Mr. HO
  explained that Pasadena began by creating public parking structures to incentivize
  development and by expediting certain projects and streamlining development to achieve
  a specific vision cheaper and sooner. Mr. MALONEY referred to Mr. Dale’s report
  regarding Segment 2 and the finding that retail only developments were marginally
  feasible. He proposed that the City focus on implementing things that were strictly under
  its control such as changing parking requirements and availability, greening pedestrian
  sidewalks, slowing traffic, and other methods to encourage development and attract
  businesses desired for the East Main Corridor. He again referred to Pasadena’s creation
  of Old Town Pasadena and suggested that the City focus on creating the environment
  that would attract businesses to develop an Old Town Alhambra. He continued to discuss
  the difference between West and East Main Street, the concerns regarding East Main
  Street’s proximity to residential neighborhoods, the economic study, creating a transitional
  area from Garfield to Chapel, and the protection of older structures such as the Forest
  Lawn Mortuary and older trees. He agreed that five story structures were too high for the
  segment, acknowledged the need for additional public outreach based on public comment,
  and that new buildings needed to be an addition to the landscape and compliant with the
  development plan. He stated that moratoriums were blunt instruments and used in cases
  of emergency. He expressed that he did not feel the Chinatown Service Center project
  was the type of development that warranted an emergency. He stated that the concerns
  of the public were valid and there needed to be ways to address them through continued
  work.

  Mayor LEE continued to discuss the need for greater public outreach to address the lack
  of accessibility to certain groups such as senior citizens and non-English speakers. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested circulating a survey in several languages to reach

  7
9-13-21
   people. Ms. LEE went on to discuss the discontent felt by residents with regards to traffic
  and overdevelopment. She stressed the need to create trust and foster support of the
  community while balancing the high population density in Alhambra. She went on to
  discuss the planning process for the Economic Analysis and Architectural Design
  Guidelines, the current projects beginning development, and projects which may be
  approved before a plan could be set in place for the East Main Corridor. She explained
  that this would affect trust within the community. She reiterated that it was necessary to
  issue a moratorium so that building projects may be dealt with fairly so that the developers
  can continue to plan their projects once the Design Guidelines have been completed. She
  stressed that she did not desire to reject development, but that it was necessary to place
  appropriate development in the right location. She stated that she did not reject the
  Chinatown Service Center, but added that their project was not the best feasible
  development for Segment 1.

  Mayor LEE motioned for a building moratorium ordinance in the East Main Corridor.
  Council continued to discuss the need for alternate methods to address incoming
  applications, and expediting discussion on the Design Guidelines. Ms. LEE continued to
  stress the need to address incoming applications and accelerating the planning process
  for the East Main Corridor.

RECESS & RECONVENE: Mayor Lee called for a recess at 10:00 p.m. and the meeting
resumed with all Councilmembers present at 10:11 p.m.

  Mayor LEE and Mr. HO continued to discuss the process to create Architectural Design
  Guidelines and the tentative completion in Spring 2022. Ms. LEE reiterated her concerns
  regarding incoming projects without a set plan for the East Main Corridor. Hearing no
  second for her motion, the Mayor concluded the discussion.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the East Main Corridor Update
  Report.

5.  DIRECTION ON A VACCINATION POLICY FOR CITY EMPLOYEES – F2M20-33,
  M2M21-117

  Human Resources Director KO delivered a staff report. Most recently the country and
  community was faced with the Delta variant of COVID-19, which became the dominant
  strain of the virus in Los Angeles County and the new Mu variant was detected with 167
  cases in Los Angeles County. Additionally, according to the Los Angeles County
  Department of Public Health, over 90% of current hospitalizations and deaths related to
  COVID-19 were among the unvaccinated persons. It was for these aforementioned
  reasons that the Los Angeles County Department of Health deemed that COVID-19
  remained a threat to public health, and to prevent its further spread, certain public health
  requirements were necessary. City staff sought direction to develop and implement a
  Vaccination Policy for all other employees, requiring all City employees to be vaccinated
  against COVID-19 with the exception of medical/religious exemption or voluntary opt out
  with weekly testing. Staff sought City Council direction to develop and implement a
  Vaccination Policy subject to meet and confer requirements with impacted employee
  groups. Due to the recent Federal action and potential new guidelines from OSHA, the
  City Manager would ensure that the City’s policy would be in compliance with those
  requirements.

  8
9-13-21
   Public Comment received via email and on file in the City Clerk’s office: Lewis
  McCammon wrote regarding the recent infection rates in Los Angeles County and
  requested that the City continue to keep residents and staff safe.

  Discussion: Council supported the Vaccination Policy. Council discussed topics such
  as moving forward to reopening, protection of the public, accessibility of testing, and
  potential Federal Government funds and programs to distribute rapid test kits.
  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and MALONEY agreed that Council should
  authorize the City Manager to appropriate American Rescue Plan Act funds for
  expenditures, unless additional Federal funding becomes available.

  Action Taken:  City Council: 1) Provided direction to the City Manager to move
  forward with the development and implementation of a Vaccination Policy for City
  Employees, subject to meet and confer requirements with impacted city employee groups,
  and undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action; and, 2) Authorized the City
  Manager to appropriate American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds to expenditures related
  to implementation of a Vaccination Policy for City Employees unless additional funds
  become available. (M2M21-117)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 20)

All other items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 6, were considered
by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

6.  DESIGNATION OF VOTING DELEGATE FOR THE LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES
  ANNUAL CONFERENCE – F2M21-13, M2M21-107

  The League of California Cities Annual Conference was scheduled for September 22nd
  through 24th in Sacramento, California. During the Conference the League conducts its
  Annual Business Meeting during which the membership considers and takes action on
  resolutions that establish future League policy. In order for the City to have a vote at the
  Annual Business Meeting, it was necessary for the City Council to designate the voting
  delegate and alternates. It was anticipated that Vice Mayor Maloney and Councilmembers
  Andrade-Stadler, Maza and Pérez would be present on Friday, September 24th when the
  Annual Business Meeting was scheduled; therefore, staff proposed that Vice Mayor
  Maloney be appointed as the Voting Delegate for the City at the Annual Business Meeting
  and Councilmembers Andrade-Stadler and Maza be appointed as Voting Delegate
  Alternates.
  Discussion:  Councilmember MALONEY informed Council of an agendized item
  which would be voted on at the League conference. Mr. Maloney reported that the item in
  question would be an amendment to the bylaws dealing with the diversity caucuses such
  as the API Caucus, Latino Caucus, African American Caucus, the LGBT Caucus, and the
  Women’s Caucus in which the caucuses would be fully integrated into the bylaws but

  9
9-13-21
   would also take away some of the autonomy of the caucuses. He informed his fellow
  Councilmembers that he planned on voting against the amendment.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the proposed appointment of Vice Mayor
  Maloney as Voting Delegate and Councilmembers Andrade-Stadler and Maza as Voting
  Delegate Alternates for the 2021 League of California Cities Conference’s Annual
  Business Meeting. (M2M21-107)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  APPROPRIATION OF ART FUNDS: ART FEATURE FOR THE AUTUMN FEST –
  F2M21-17, M2M21-108

  The Arts and Cultural Events Committee was excited to bring public art to the community
  of Alhambra. A committee member found and brought this idea to the committee in an
  effort to get more involved. The project, designed by artist Yeu Q. Nguyen, entailed the
  installation of a banner made entirely of reused materials donated by people and
  organizations. The HOPE banner would ask community members to write a note about
  their hopes and dreams for Alhambra and tie it to the banner. By building this living piece
  of art, the project would strengthen sense of community and unity in Alhambra. This HOPE
  banner would be installed at Alhambra Park for four weeks and would be featured at the
  City’s Autumn Festival.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council appropriated funds from the Art in Public Places Fund
  for Yeu Q. Nguyen's HOPE Banner project, which included design, construction, and
  installation; approved an agreement by and between the City of Alhambra and Yeu Q
  Nguyen's for an amount not to exceed $1,500; subject to final language approved by the
  City Manager and City Attorney; and directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the City Council's action. (M2M21-108)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  REQUEST CARRYOVER AND APPROPRIATION OF GOLF COURSE CLUBHOUSE
  FUNDS – F2M21-17, M2M21-109

  In the adoption of the fiscal year 2020-21 budget, staff budgeted funds for the removal
  and replacement of four HVAC units at Almansor Court. In March of 2021, a Notice Inviting
  Bids was circulated for the Almansor Court HVAC Replacement Project. One bid was
  received on April 15, 2021. On April 26, 2021, staff recommended that the one bid be
  rejected and that a new Notice Inviting Bid be circulated. On April 26, 2021, City Council
  approved a Notice Inviting Bids for the same Project. On May 13, 2021, the City Clerk

  10
9-13-21
   received four bids for the Project. On June 14, 2021 Thermal Air Conditioning Inc. was
  awarded the contract for $73,490.00. The Almansor Court HVAC Replacement Project
  was completed on July 16, 2021.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized a carryover in the amount of $73,490.00
  from the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Golf Course Clubhouse Fund to the Fiscal Year 2021-
  2022 Golf Course Clubhouse Fund for the replacement of HVAC units at Almansor Court;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-
  109)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: FY 2020-21 SB1 STREET REHABILITATION PROJECT –
  F2M20-35, N2M21-79, C2M21-49, M2M21-111

  This project included asphalt pavement resurfacing of 24 street segments; repair and
  replacement of approximately 16,000 square feet of broken and off grade sidewalk;
  upgrades or installation of ADA ramps within the project limits; repair of approximately
  3,850 linear feet of broken and off-grade curb and gutters; broken and off-grade alley
  sections and driveway approaches; and repair/installation of concrete cross-gutters in
  residential areas bounded by Valley Blvd. on the north, Ramona Rd. North on the south,
  Atlantic Blvd. on the east and Fremont Ave. on the west. A Notice Inviting Bids was
  authorized by the City Council on June 14, 2021 and on August 5, 2021 the City Clerk

a City sponsored event. Councilmember PÉREZ stated that while she supported the event, she

would like more information regarding logistics. City Manager BINNQUIST stated that if this was
agreed upon by Council, then it would be added to the Strategic Plan and that a new Strategic
Plan would be circulated to Council for approval at a City Council meeting. Councilmember
ANDRADE-STADLER supported the idea of the event, but did not support altering priorities on

approach the Strategic Plan in the future. He also stated that he would support Ms. Lee in hosting
